## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Antajātaka* (Ja 295), titled in English translation as *The Worst*, is a narrative discourse within the canonical Pali *Jātaka* collection [SuttaCentral]. According to its opening narrative framing, the story commences with the verse incipit "Like to a bull" and was delivered by the Buddha under the same setting and concerning the same figures as the immediately preceding discourse [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral documents four translations across four modern languages [SuttaCentral]. None of the secondary literature passages in the dossier directly address the text, having been captured through accidental substring matches with unrelated titles.

In computational text-reuse analyses by DharmaNexus, the *Antajātaka* shares five matching segments (totaling 481 characters) with the Pali commentary, the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (*Dutiyo bhāgo*), with the longest correspondence spanning §1.1–2.4 of the text and §2872–2878 of the commentary [DharmaNexus]. Cross-linguistically, DharmaNexus reports 11 automated segment alignments between the *Antajātaka* and the Sanskrit *Saṅghabhedavastu* (part 2), with a peak match score of 75 (such as §0.1 matching §6598), representing an uncurated machine alignment rather than an established narrative parallel [DharmaNexus].
